summary: Locked burst/partial-hourly credit preventing subscription renewal and causing provisional invoice hold
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that a locked/held partial hourly credit from a recent rate-tier change has prevented their monthly subscription renewal from completing. The billing system shows a provisional hold on the March invoice and a "locked credit" line that is not being applied. Impact: subscription renewal failed (payment blocked by provisional invoice), customer-facing services saw brief rate-limited behavior during renewal attempts, and the finance team is requesting immediate remediation to avoid service interruption on Monday. Environment: production, dedicated plan, us-east cluster.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Customer changed rate tier on 2026-03-11 17:20 UTC (billing change).
2) Several microbatch embedding jobs and chat requests ran between 17:30-18:30 UTC (high concurrency).
3) Automated hourly credit accumulator ran at 18:00 UTC and showed a "partial/locked" credit row for the hour.
4) Billing engine created a provisional invoice on 2026-03-12 which included the locked credit as a pending line item; because the credit was in pending state the invoice remained on hold and renewal failed.

Observed logs/attachments: billing_postback_2026-03-11.log (provided by customer), invoice_snapshot_2026-03-12.csv (customer), screenshots of console billing UI showing locked credit row.

Customer request: Remove the hold or apply the provisional credit so renewal can proceed, confirm root cause and provide mitigation to prevent recurrence.
comments: 2026-03-12 09:07 - Support: Acknowledged ticket and requested the invoice snapshot, recent postback logs, and timestamp of the rate-tier change. Escalated to Billing team.

2026-03-12 10:44 - Customer (Kiln Analytics): Uploaded invoice_snapshot_2026-03-12.csv and billing_postback_2026-03-11.log. Confirmed rate-tier change at 2026-03-11T17:20:12Z. Customer says renewal attempt was at 2026-03-12T01:05:00Z local time.

2026-03-12 11:30 - Billing (Rohan Patel): Initial triage suggests out-of-order postbacks + hourly accumulator mismatch. Requested SRE to check postback ordering and accumulator state for org_id=org_ki_9842.

2026-03-12 13:05 - SRE (Diego Alvarez): Found three postbacks for the same hour arriving with non-monotonic timestamps (postback ordering gaps). Hourly accumulator recorded a "partial_credit_locked" state while reconciliation window was open. Created INT-7312 to track accumulator re-run request.

2026-03-12 15:20 - Billing (Rohan Patel): Applied a provisional manual credit of USD 1,120 to clear the hold so renewal could proceed. Noted downstream fix required: idempotent ordering for postback ingestion and a compensating reconciliation job.
2026-03-12 16:00 - Customer: Confirmed payment processed and subscription renewed. Asked for confirmation that peak-hour bulk jobs won't re-lock credits on next change.
2026-03-13 09:12 - Support: Provided temporary mitigation steps and ETA for permanent fix. Scheduled a follow-up by 2026-03-16 after accumulator patch and enhanced postback dedupe deploy.

2026-03-14 08:45 - Billing (Rohan Patel): Deployed accumulator reconciliation patch to backfill the locked hour for org_ki_9842; reprocessed the postbacks in correct order and cleared residual pending rows. Confirmed accounting adjustment recorded in ledger. Marking ticket resolved pending acceptance.
2026-03-14 09:10 - Customer (Kiln Analytics): Acknowledged resolution and asked for a small postmortem and recommendation to reduce recurrence risk.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Out-of-order usage postbacks during a high-concurrency window caused the hourly accumulator to mark a partial credit as locked because the final reconciliation event was delayed.

Hypothesis 2: Rate-tier change triggered an intermediate recalculation that created a transient credit row which the provisional invoice logic treats as pending until accumulator confirms final state.

Evidence: SRE logs show three postback events for org_ki_9842 between 2026-03-11T17:29:31Z and 2026-03-11T17:31:02Z with non-monotonic sequence numbers. Hourly accumulator state machine transitioned to 'pending_locked_credit' and did not progress to 'confirmed' due to a reconciliation race condition.
Temporary mitigation tested: Manually reordering postbacks before running accumulator re-run corrected the credit amount and allowed the invoice to be marked payable.
Related systems to review: postback ingestion queue, hourly accumulator state machine, provisional invoice hold logic, and UI path that surfaces 'locked credit' lines to customers.
resolution_notes: Applied manual provisional credit of USD 1,120 on 2026-03-12 15:20 UTC to allow immediate renewal; customer confirmed subscription renewed same day.

Deployed accumulator reconciliation patch on 2026-03-14 08:30 UTC that: (a) reprocessed buffered postbacks in correct order for the affected hour, (b) moved 'partial_credit_locked' -> 'confirmed' when totals matched, and (c) emitted a clearing transaction to ledger. See INT-7312 for runbook and logs.
Accounting adjustment: billing ledger entry BLG-2026-03-14-9842 created to reflect applied provisional credit and reconcile against invoiced amount. Finance notified for audit.

Follow-up actions: (1) Add deduplication and ordering guard to postback ingestion (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/1483), (2) Add a 5-minute reconciliation window before provisional invoice hold is escalated to payment blockage, (3) Create a console alert to surface 'locked credit' state to account owners and to internal billing team earlier.
Customer follow-up: Sent postmortem summary and recommended guardrail changes to Kiln Analytics on 2026-03-14; scheduled review call for 2026-03-18.
